items.followUp: What is xerophthalmia, and which vitamin deficiency causes it?

rubric.why: Identifies the vitamin deficiency associated with night-blindness.
rubric.description: Night-blindness results from vitamin A deficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking night-blindness with vitamin A deficiency.

rubric.why: States the main effect of night-blindness.
rubric.description: A person has difficulty seeing in dim light or at night.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing impaired vision in dim light or at night.

modelAnswer: Night-blindness is a condition commonly caused by deficiency of vitamin A.
A person with night-blindness has difficulty seeing in dim light or at night.

items.followUp: What are dietary fibres, and how do they help prevent constipation?

rubric.why: Identifies insoluble dietary fibre as indigestible plant material, such as cellulose.
rubric.description: Insoluble dietary fibres are indigestible plant materials, including cellulose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying fibre as indigestible plant material or naming cellulose.

rubric.why: States the defining property of insoluble fibre.
rubric.description: These fibres do not dissolve in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the fibres are insoluble in water.

modelAnswer: Insoluble dietary fibres are indigestible plant materials, such as cellulose, that do not dissolve in water.

items.followUp: Name and briefly describe five career fields related to biology.

rubric.why: Gives one valid biology-related career and its role.
rubric.description: Medicine involves diagnosing and treating diseases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for medicine or a related medical career.

rubric.why: Gives a second valid career field and its role.
rubric.description: Agriculture applies biology to crop production and improvement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for agriculture or crop science.

rubric.why: Gives a third valid career field and its role.
rubric.description: Animal husbandry or veterinary science concerns the care and improvement of animals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for animal husbandry, livestock work or veterinary science.

rubric.why: Gives a fourth valid career field and its role.
rubric.description: Fisheries includes fish breeding, farming and management.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for fisheries or aquaculture.

rubric.why: Gives a fifth valid career field and its role.
rubric.description: Forestry concerns the management of forests; biotechnology is another valid biology career.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for forestry or another distinct valid biology-related career.

modelAnswer: Medicine: biologists can become doctors and diagnose and treat diseases.
Agriculture: biology is used to grow and improve crops.
Animal husbandry: biology is applied to the breeding and care of farm animals; veterinarians also treat animals.
Fisheries: biologists work in fish breeding, fish farming and fisheries management.
Forestry: biologists help manage and conserve forests.

items.followUp: Draw a labelled diagram of a mitochondrion and describe its structure.

rubric.why: The diagram must show the ribosome's two subunits.
rubric.description: Draws and labels the large and small subunits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a recognisable two-subunit ribosome diagram with both labels.

rubric.why: The diagram should show a key feature associated with the ribosome.
rubric.description: Shows and labels an mRNA strand passing between or beneath the subunits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a labelled mRNA strand in the diagram.

rubric.why: Identifies the materials that make up ribosomes.
rubric.description: Ribosomes are made of ribosomal RNA and proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ribosomes contain RNA and proteins.

rubric.why: States the key function that explains the ribosome's structure.
rubric.description: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying protein synthesis as their function.

modelAnswer: Draw two joined, rounded subunits, with the larger subunit above the smaller one.
Draw a strand passing beneath or between the subunits and label it mRNA; label the two parts large subunit and small subunit.
Ribosomes are small, non-membranous structures made of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.
They consist of a large and a small subunit and are the sites of protein synthesis.

items.followUp: Describe five ways in which deforestation can affect the environment.

rubric.why: Names a major effect of removing trees.
rubric.description: Deforestation increases soil erosion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for soil erosion or loss of topsoil.

rubric.why: Names a further effect linked to reduced water absorption by forests.
rubric.description: Deforestation can increase the risk of flooding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for floods or flooding.

rubric.why: Recognises the effect of forest loss on climate.
rubric.description: Deforestation contributes to global warming or climate change.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for global warming, climate change or rising temperature.

rubric.why: Recognises harm to organisms and ecosystems.
rubric.description: Deforestation destroys habitats and can reduce biodiversity or cause extinctions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for habitat loss, reduced biodiversity or extinction of species.

rubric.why: Identifies another environmental consequence of forest removal.
rubric.description: Deforestation can disrupt the water cycle, reduce rainfall or lead to drought and desertification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid effect on the water cycle, rainfall or land.

modelAnswer: Deforestation increases soil erosion because tree roots no longer hold the soil together.
It can increase the risk of floods.
It contributes to global warming and climate change.
It destroys habitats, reduces biodiversity and may lead to the extinction of species.
It disrupts the water cycle and can reduce rainfall, causing drought or desertification.

items.followUp: Write the balanced equation for photosynthesis and state the conditions needed for it.

rubric.why: Includes the correct reactants and products in the photosynthesis equation.
rubric.description: Carbon dioxide and water form glucose and oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct reactants and products.

rubric.why: Checks that the chemical equation is balanced.
rubric.description: Gives the balanced equation with coefficients 6, 6, 1 and 6.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced chemical equation.

rubric.why: Identifies the light energy required for the process.
rubric.description: Photosynthesis uses sunlight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for sunlight or light energy.

rubric.why: Identifies the pigment that captures light energy.
rubric.description: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy for photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for chlorophyll.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.
6CO₂ + 6H₂O —(light and chlorophyll)→ C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
Sunlight provides the energy for the process.
Chlorophyll absorbs the light energy.

items.followUp: Compare vitamins D and B₁ by giving a function, a source and a deficiency effect for each.

rubric.why: Provides a correct definition of vitamins.
rubric.description: Vitamins are organic compounds required in small amounts for normal growth and health.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing vitamins as organic compounds needed in small quantities.

rubric.why: States an important function or deficiency effect of vitamin A.
rubric.description: Vitamin A is needed for normal vision; its deficiency can cause night-blindness.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct vitamin A function or deficiency effect.

rubric.why: Names a valid source of vitamin A.
rubric.description: Sources include carrots, milk, eggs and fish-liver oil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid vitamin A source.

rubric.why: States an important function or deficiency effect of vitamin C.
rubric.description: Vitamin C supports collagen formation and wound healing; its deficiency causes scurvy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct vitamin C function or deficiency effect.

rubric.why: Names a valid source of vitamin C.
rubric.description: Citrus fruits and fresh vegetables are sources of vitamin C.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid vitamin C source.

modelAnswer: Vitamins are organic compounds required in small amounts for normal growth and health.
Vitamin A is needed for normal vision and healthy epithelial tissues; deficiency may cause night-blindness.
Sources of vitamin A include carrots, milk, eggs and fish-liver oil.
Vitamin C is needed for collagen formation and wound healing; its deficiency causes scurvy, which may include bleeding gums.
Citrus fruits and fresh vegetables are sources of vitamin C.

items.followUp: Describe the structure and functions of white blood cells and plasma.

rubric.why: Describes the characteristic shape of red blood cells.
rubric.description: Red blood cells are biconcave discs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying their biconcave disc shape.

rubric.why: States the main role of red blood cells.
rubric.description: Their haemoglobin carries oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking haemoglobin or red blood cells with oxygen transport.

rubric.why: Describes the nature of platelets.
rubric.description: Platelets are small cell fragments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying platelets as small cell fragments.

rubric.why: States the key function of platelets.
rubric.description: Platelets help blood to clot and prevent excessive bleeding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying blood clotting as the function of platelets.

modelAnswer: Red blood cells are biconcave discs containing haemoglobin, which carries oxygen around the body.
Mature red blood cells in mammals do not have a nucleus.
Platelets are small cell fragments in the blood.
They help blood to clot and prevent excessive bleeding.
